propositions: test_slow_but_progressing_remote_is_not_aborted uses a 15-second production window and 15-second real loopback server, causing multi-second test overhead; the contract requires sustained bytes above floor for one complete window, not production-scale elapsed time

test_read_retried_then_terminal uses a one-second call timeout plus real 2s/4s backoff sleeps across three child processes, taking ~9 seconds; the contract is exactly three attempts, the logical retry schedule, and process cleanup proof, not elapsed seconds
snapshot stall test must inject a one-second low-speed window while preserving real loopback socket and above-floor byte pacing for more than one complete window, retaining the non-stall assertion

ACLI subprocess timeout test must inject sub-second call/grace/drain values through existing seams, record logical backoff [2,4] without sleeping real retry delays, and retain exactly _MAX_ATTEMPTS real child sessions
Every PID spawned by the ACLI read sentinel must be recorded and polled absent after terminal failure to prove no child or process group survives
Production timeout, stall, grace, drain, attempt, and backoff defaults must remain unchanged with no modifications to production code
